entries.summary: Your phone as a heads-up display for your car: lay it flat on the dashboard and read your GPS speed on the windscreen.
facts: Number, Gauge arc, Fighter, Centre bar
At dusk, at night, on cloudy days

steps.text: Open HUD mode: tap HUD mode on Home or in Styles, use the HUD mode tile in Quick Settings, or long-press the app's icon. The first time, a short setup asks one question per step.
Pick your look: Number, Gauge arc, Fighter or Centre bar, drawn by Horizon (free), Glass, Pulse or Vector, in the style's own colour or in Lime, Cyan, Ice white, Amber or Violet.

Say how the phone lies: top edge to the glass, top edge to you, or upright in a holder. Lying flat, your speed is drawn flipped, so the windscreen reflects it the right way round; in a holder it reads straight, with no flip.

While parked, lay the phone flat on the dashboard in front of the wheel, screen up, where it can't slide and clear of the airbags. Then drive and leave it alone: once you've stopped, tap it once for Exit and Flip.

cta.title: Try it in your browser
cta.text: The try page runs HUD mode too: pick a look and watch it with your real GPS speed or a demo drive, before you install anything.
cta.label: Try HUD mode in your browser

what: HUD mode turns your phone into a heads-up display for your car. It fills the screen with your speed alone, drawn flipped, so the windscreen in front of you reflects it the right way round: a car HUD with no extra box on the dashboard.
Four looks, four styles. Number, Gauge arc, Fighter and Centre bar, drawn by Horizon for free, or by Glass, Pulse and Vector with the style, Speedometer Plus or a 24-hour trial.
Your colour. Keep the style's own colour, or pick Lime, Cyan, Ice white, Amber or Violet, whichever reads best on your glass.
More on the glass. Add the clock, the trip, your heading and a speed warning: above the limit you set, the speed turns red and the phone beeps once. The app doesn't know the road's limit.
Opens in your car. Switch on Open by itself in my car and pick your car once: HUD mode opens when the phone joins its Bluetooth.
Looks after your phone. On a low battery a small Plug in mark shows once per drive. If the phone gets hot, HUD mode dims, then pauses to let it cool down, and comes back by itself.

compare.title: Seeing double?
compare.text: A windscreen has two glass surfaces, and each one reflects the phone, so a bare windscreen shows your speed twice. A HUD film on the inside of the glass, or a HUD reflector plate on the dashboard, leaves one sharp image.

before.label: Without film
before.alt: Glass's Number HUD on a bare windscreen at night: 60 km/h, the clock, trip and heading each show twice, a faint copy just above

after.label: With film
after.alt: The same HUD with a HUD film on the windscreen: one sharp image of 60 km/h, the clock, trip and heading

compare.caption: Drag the handle: a bare windscreen on the left, one with a HUD film on the right.

tip.label: Before you drive
tip.title: Set it up while parked
tip.text: Lay the phone where it can't slide, clear of the airbags, and don't touch it while you drive. Check that your country allows a phone on the dashboard.

notes: HUD mode reads best at dusk, at night and on cloudy days. In bright sun the reflection is faint.
It has no menus and no ads while you drive: one tap shows Exit and Flip.
Your speed comes from GPS while HUD mode is open, and it never leaves the phone. Until the phone has a fix, the glass shows NO GPS.
Each HUD style's page has an Original | HUD switch: Horizon, Glass, Pulse and Vector.
entries.artAlt: A phone lies flat on a car's dashboard at night, showing HUD mode's speed upside down, and the windscreen above it reflects the same HUD the right way round: 87 km/h on a green gauge arc, with the time, trip and heading, over a rainy city street

entries.name: The big gauge
entries.summary: One dial, three jobs: power, CPU clock or GPS speed.
what: The big gauge shows one of three things: power, CPU clock or GPS speed. The digits above the needle show the same value as the needle.
how: Pick the mode in Customize → Big gauge, tap the gauge on your home screen, or use the Big gauge tile in Quick Settings to switch. Each style keeps its own mode.

entries.name: Big gauge tile
entries.summary: A Quick Settings tile that switches the big gauge on any phone.
what: Some launchers, Samsung's included, don't pass taps on to the wallpaper, so tapping the big gauge does nothing there. The Big gauge tile in Quick Settings switches the mode on every phone, in the same order: power, CPU clock, GPS speed.
Its subtitle shows the mode the gauge is in now. It skips modes your phone can't show, like CPU clock on phones that don't allow reading it.
how: On Android 13 and later, Settings → Big gauge tile → Add puts it in your Quick Settings for you.
Or open the Quick Settings editor and drag Big gauge into your tiles.

entries.name: Power mode
entries.summary: Watts going into or out of the battery.
what: In power mode the needle shows the watts going into the battery (to the right, while charging) or out of it (to the left, with a minus).
how: Plug in your charger and watch the needle swing right: a quick way to see how fast a charger really is.
facts: Tap the gauge or the Big gauge tile

steps.text: Pick Power in Customize → Big gauge, tap the gauge on your home screen, or use the Big gauge tile.
Plug in your charger and watch the needle swing right: a quick way to see how fast a charger really is.
On battery the needle swings left, with a minus.

gauge.label: Power gauge
gauge.offText: On battery: the needle swings left, with a minus.

entries.name: CPU clock mode
entries.summary: How fast the processor runs, as a share of its top speed.
what: In CPU clock mode the needle shows how hard your phone's processor is being pushed: how fast its cores are running right now, as a percentage of the fastest they can run.

A phone's processor has several cores, often of different sizes, and each one speeds up and slows down many times a second. The wallpaper reads every core's current speed and its top speed, adds them up, and shows the first total as a share of the second. A core with nothing to report counts as zero, so a phone resting on the home screen reads low, and a game or a big download pushes the needle up.
It takes a reading once a second and smooths it over about three seconds, so the needle sweeps like a real rev counter instead of twitching.
how: The percentage is about speed, not how busy the processor is. A phone saving battery can run busy cores slowly, so 40% doesn't mean 40% busy.

Some phones don't allow apps to read the CPU clock. On those, the gauge shows -- instead of a number, and it does the same when a phone reports a speed that can't be real, such as a core running faster than its own top speed. Use power or GPS speed instead.

entries.name: GPS speed mode
entries.summary: Your speed in km/h or mph, with a red mark at your top speed.
what: In GPS speed mode the needle shows your speed. A red mark shows the top speed of the current drive.

GPS speed needs your precise location while the wallpaper is on screen, and so do the trip, heading, altitude and Map widgets. Only the Weather and Map widgets send a rough location, never your exact point.
how: Choose GPS speed in Customize → Big gauge; the app explains why it needs location, then Android asks. Pick "Precise" when it does.
Switch between km/h and mph in Customize → Units or in Settings → Speed unit: the unit is the same in every style, so changing it changes them all.
If location is off for the app, the gauge can't read your speed: allow precise location in the app's settings.

entries.name: Signal
entries.summary: Top left: your mobile signal, from 0 to 4 bars.
what: The small gauge at the top left shows your mobile signal, from 0 to 4 bars.

entries.name: RAM
entries.summary: Top right: how much of the phone's memory is in use.
what: The small gauge at the top right shows how much of the phone's memory is in use.

entries.name: Wi-Fi
entries.summary: Bottom left: Wi-Fi strength, status and link speed.
what: The Wi-Fi gauge shows the strength of your Wi-Fi signal.
Under it, a status line reads CONNECTED, NO NETWORK, MOBILE DATA or DISABLED. When connected, it also shows the link speed in Mbps.

entries.name: Battery
entries.summary: Bottom right: how full your battery is.
what: The battery gauge shows how full your battery is. Its LOW light comes on at the low battery level, and the green bolt lights while the phone charges.

entries.name: Battery temperature
entries.summary: The little dial: from cold (C) to hot (H).
what: The small dial inside the battery gauge shows the battery's temperature, from the low temperature (C) to the high one (H).
how: Set what counts as low and high in Customize → Warning lamps; the warning lights use the same limits.

entries.name: Low battery light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: the battery is at or below your low level.
what: Lights when the battery is at or below the low battery level: 15 % unless you change it.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Low battery switches the light off, and Low battery level changes the limit.

entries.name: Bluetooth light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: Bluetooth is on.
what: Lights while Bluetooth is on.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Bluetooth switches it off.

entries.name: High temperature light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: your phone's battery is hotter than the limit you set, 45 °C unless you change it.
what: The high temperature light, the high temp light for short, is one of the warning lights on the big gauge. It reads the temperature of your phone's battery, the same reading as the little C-to-H dial in the battery gauge, and lights the moment it climbs past your high limit. Once the battery cools back down to the limit, it goes out by itself.

It's about your phone, not your car. The light on your car's own dashboard, usually a thermometer standing in waves, warns that the engine is too hot; this one never knows the engine's temperature. If the car's light comes on, believe the car.

A phone heats up in a car faster than you'd think. Sun through the windscreen, fast charging, navigation and GPS, a bright screen and a thick case all add heat, and the top of a dashboard in summer gets far hotter than the air in the car.

When it lights, move the phone out of direct sun, unplug it or stop fast charging for a while, close the apps you aren't using and take off the case. Phones protect themselves too: a hot phone dims its screen, slows down and may pause charging until it cools.

The limit is yours. 45 °C is already warm for a phone battery, but you can set the limit anywhere up to 70 °C, or switch the light off. The battery dial moves with it: C is your low limit and H your high one, so the dial reaches H just as the light comes on.

In HUD mode the phone lies on the dashboard in the sun, so the app keeps an eye on the heat for you: it turns the HUD down first, pauses it to let the phone cool if the heat keeps climbing, then carries on by itself.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → High temperature level sets the limit: anywhere from 1 °C above the low temperature limit up to 70 °C.
Switch the light off in the same place to hide it; the battery's little dial still shows the temperature.

tip.label: In the car
tip.title: The car's own light comes first
tip.text: If the high temperature light on your car's real dashboard comes on, the engine is overheating: pull over where it's safe, switch the engine off and let it cool before you check anything. Never open a hot radiator cap.

entries.name: Low temperature light
entries.summary: On the big gauge: the battery is colder than your limit.
what: Lights when the battery is colder than the low temperature: 0 °C unless you change it.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Low temperature level sets the limit.

entries.name: Charging bolt
entries.summary: On the battery gauge: the phone is charging.
what: The green bolt on the battery gauge lights while the phone charges.
how: Customize → Warning lamps → Charging switches it off.

entries.name: LOW light
entries.summary: On the battery gauge: the battery is low.
what: The LOW light on the battery gauge comes on at the low battery level.

entries.name: Wi-Fi ON light
entries.summary: On the Wi-Fi gauge: green on Wi-Fi, yellow on mobile data.
what: The ON light on the Wi-Fi gauge is green while you're on Wi-Fi and yellow on mobile data.

entries.name: Date and time
entries.summary: The LCD under the big gauge.
what: The LCD under the big gauge shows the date and the time.
how: In Customize → Clock you can set the time format (12 h, 24 h or the phone's), whether seconds show, the date order, and the time and date separators. The time format and the seconds are the same in every style, so changing them changes every style; the date order and the separators are each style's own.

entries.name: Settings
entries.summary: The app's settings, and each style's own in Customize.
what: Tap the gear at the top of the home screen for the app's settings. Each style's own settings are in Customize, on the home screen and on the Styles screen.
how: Wallpaper: the style in use, Motion and battery (Saver, Balanced or Smooth) and the Big gauge tile.

Every style: the speed unit and the clock (12 or 24 hours, and seconds), the same in every style, and Copy settings to all styles, which gives every style one style's big gauge, units, clock, lamps and needle motion. Each style keeps its own layout and look.
Permissions: GPS speed (location) and Music, calls and messages (notification access).
Previews and feedback: live previews and vibration.
Widgets: the second clock's city, your daily step goal, and Tilt level, which sets level for the Tilt widget with the phone in its mount.
Purchases: Speedometer Plus (every style and no ads) and Restore purchases.
Signed in to VHub, your settings follow you: on every phone you sign in on, and in the VHub menu at the top right of vgraphics.gr. Without signing in, they stay on this phone.

Privacy: Ad choices (where your region requires it) and the privacy policy. Help: Help & ideas, which sends VGraphics a ticket (with a screenshot if you like) and shows our answers, Rate us, which opens the app on Google Play, and News by email. About: the Guide and the licences.

Customize, for one style: the big gauge's mode and top-speed mark, units, clock, warning lamps, music, calls and messages, and the look (colours, glow, background, needle feel and the start-up sweep). Changes show at once in the preview, and Reset puts the style's defaults back.

Add to home screen, at the foot of Customize, opens the two home-screen widgets drawn in the style in use: Speedometer clock and Speedometer music. Tap one and Android asks where to put it; where your home screen can't add it that way, the card tells you to touch and hold your home screen, tap Widgets and find Speedometer. Both widgets follow the style you use, so they change when you pick another style or change its colours.

entries.name: Setting it as your wallpaper
entries.title: Setting it as your wallpaper · Speedometer Live Wallpaper
entries.summary: Set as wallpaper, confirm, done; and how to get it back.
what: Open the app and tap Set as wallpaper, then confirm on the preview. The button turns amber and reads On your home screen: the dashboard is now your wallpaper.
how: If you force-stop the app or clear its data, Android puts your old wallpaper back. Open the app and tap Set as wallpaper again.
The wallpaper never shows ads.
notes: Speedometer Live Wallpaper is for Android phones and tablets only: iPhones don't allow live wallpapers from other apps.

entries.name: The Styles screen
entries.summary: All 19 styles, drawn live: use one, buy one, pick its layout, or build your own with 48 widgets.
what: Open the app and tap Styles. Your styles come first, then the rest, each drawn live by the wallpaper itself with its name and its state: In use, Free, Owned or Locked. Tap one for its page: a live demo you can pause, Power, CPU and Speed buttons, its description and its layouts.
how: Tap Use this style to switch: the wallpaper changes at once. If Speedometer isn't your live wallpaper yet, a sheet offers Set as wallpaper, so you see the style on your home screen; Not now keeps the style for later. The same sheet comes up once after you buy a style or Speedometer Plus, or start a 24 h trial with a short video, as soon as Google Play's window or the video has closed.

Tap Buy to buy a style once through Google Play, or Every style for Speedometer Plus, a monthly or yearly subscription: every style, including the styles still to come, and no ads. Google Play shows the price for your country.

Under Layouts, pick one of the style's own, a ready-made one, one of yours (Mine) or one from the market, and tap Use this layout. Edit layout opens it in the layout builder: one of yours changes in every style, any other becomes your own copy and the original stays as it is. New layout, the + card at the end of the row, starts one of your own: from the layout on show, or blank.

Show QR for this look on the try page of vgraphics.gr puts a style and layout in a QR code: scan it with your phone and the app opens on that style, the layout shown as if you had picked it. Tap Use this layout to keep it, or Buy for a style you don't own yet.

In the layout builder, Add widget brings in a widget, a drag moves it and its red handle resizes it, and Bring to front and Send to back stack widgets that overlap. The chips under the layout list its layers, front first: drag one by its handle (or hold it and drag) to move that widget up or down the stack. The padlock toggle beside a chosen widget's name locks it in place while you arrange the rest. Pinch the layout, or use the buttons in its corner, to zoom in on the details. Preview in shows it in any style, even one you don't own yet. Save layout keeps it under Mine, and the style's page comes back with your new layout on show, the Layouts row scrolled to its card (with animations off, it jumps there); Save and publish to the market shares it.

Add widget lists the 48 widgets by section, each with a live preview of how the style draws it: Gauges (the main gauge, battery, RAM, signal, Wi-Fi, lights, the phone's status meters, a backplate and more), On the road (trip distance, average and top speed, drive time, a trip computer, a 0–100 timer, G-force, the odometer, climb rate, the Map and Next turn), Where you are (heading, altitude, tilt, sunrise and sunset, the moon, weather, air pressure), The phone (battery time, data speed, storage, steps today), Your day (the clock, date, the date and time together and a second clock, next alarm and event, Now Playing, music buttons, volume, calls and messages) and Your photos (a photo frame, an instant print and a round photo). Every style shows every widget, each in its own look, and a widget reads only while it's on your wallpaper.

The Map comes with Speedometer Pro: the OpenStreetMap streets round you, heading-up and zooming out as you speed up, as a round nav screen or a strip, in each style's own colours. It covers Greece for now.

A widget that needs your location, your steps or your calendar asks Android for it when you add it; the weather asks only for your approximate location. Pick the second clock's city, your step goal and the tilt's level in Settings, under Widgets.

Now Playing, the music buttons, Calls and messages and Next turn need notification access: the app takes you there when you add one. In the previews they show a sample song and counts; on your wallpaper, until the access is on, Now Playing reads MUSIC AND CALLS ARE OFF and Calls and messages reads CALLS AND MESSAGES ARE OFF.
notes: If a payment is still pending, or Google Play isn't available, the screen tells you.

Only the Weather and Map widgets send anything: a rough location, never your exact point. The weather's, rounded to about 10 km, goes to MET Norway (api.met.no) for the forecast; the map asks our map host for the squares of about 2 km round you. Weather data from MET Norway, under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data and CC BY 4.0.

The music buttons work where your home screen passes taps to the wallpaper; Samsung's home screen doesn't. There, add the Speedometer music widget to your home screen (Customize → Add to home screen): its buttons work on every home screen.

entries.name: Classic style
entries.summary: Free: the 2016 dashboard with five gauges, four lights and an LCD clock.
what: Classic is the original 2016 dashboard on a brushed-metal background: the big gauge with signal and RAM behind its shoulders, Wi-Fi and battery below, four warning lights and the LCD clock.
It's free, like Steel and Graphite, and it's the style you start with. It never asks for notification access.

entries.name: Future style
entries.summary: The 2016 chrome cluster, rebuilt, as a one-time purchase.
what: Future is one big chrome dial that follows the same three modes as Classic (power, CPU clock or GPS speed), with the value in its blue glass hub and battery and RAM arcs at the bottom.
Above it, the clock and date. Below it, the music area, the Bluetooth and Wi-Fi status, and how many calls you missed and messages you haven't read.
In landscape, on tablets and unfolded foldables, it becomes the 2016 two-dial cluster: the big gauge on the left, mobile signal and battery temperature on the right, music in the middle.
how: Buy it once on the Styles screen: a one-time purchase that stays yours. Or get it with every other style through Speedometer Plus, a subscription.
Tap the dial, or use the Big gauge tile, to switch its mode.
The music and the call and message counts need notification access.

entries.name: Music, calls and messages
entries.summary: In any style: the song that's playing, music buttons, missed calls and new messages.
what: In any style, the Now Playing widget shows the song that's playing, with its cover, the music buttons control it, and the Calls and messages widget shows how many calls you missed and messages you haven't read. Add them in the layout builder. The Future style has the song, the media volume and the counts built in.

For that, Android has to give the app notification access. Android warns that an app with it could read all your notifications: this one only reads the song that's playing, counts missed calls and messages, and, for the Next turn widget, reads the next turn while Google Maps guides you. What it reads never leaves your phone.
how: The app asks when you add one of those widgets in the layout builder, or after you pick or buy Future. You can also turn it on in Settings → Permissions, or in Future's Customize → Music, calls and messages → Notification access.
Without access, Now Playing and Future's music area read MUSIC AND CALLS ARE OFF, and Calls and messages reads CALLS AND MESSAGES ARE OFF. Future's volume bar still works.
You can turn the access off any time in Android's settings.
The Speedometer music home-screen widget uses the same access. Without it, the widget reads Tap to show your music, and a tap opens the access screen.
notes: Calls and messages are counted from their notifications, never from your call log or your messages. Without these widgets or Next turn, no style but Future asks for notification access.

entries.name: Restoring your styles on a new phone
entries.title: Restoring styles on a new phone · Speedometer Live Wallpaper
entries.summary: Bought once, back by themselves on any phone with the same Google account.
what: Every style you buy is a one-time purchase tied to your Google account. The app checks your purchases with Google Play every time you open it, so on a new phone signed in with the same account, they come back by themselves.
Speedometer Plus is a subscription on your Google account, and signed in to VHub, every device of your VHub account gets it too.
how: Install the app on the new phone, open it once, then pick your style on the Styles screen. If one is missing, tap Settings → Restore purchases.
Your purchases are also remembered on the phone, so the wallpaper never waits for Google Play.
notes: A refunded purchase is removed the next time the app checks.
